name: Flock
description: A pad made of small gliding voices: every key calls a flock that flies in, hovers around the note and scatters when the key is let go.

params.name: Birds
params.description: How many voices each key calls. One is a single whistle; more make a cloud around the note without getting louder. A change is heard from the next key press.

params.name: Gather
params.description: How long the voices take to fly in and settle on the note: a quick swoop when short, a slow swell when long. A change is heard from the next key press.

params.name: From
params.description: Where the voices fly in from: under the note, over it, or from both sides at once. A change is heard from the next key press.

params.name: Stray
params.description: How far the voices roam around the note once they are there. At zero they settle into one clean unison; higher smears the pitch into a wide cloud.

params.name: Flutter
params.description: How fast the voices move about: the speed of their roaming around the note, of their drift from side to side and of their calls.

params.name: Tone
params.description: The voice of each bird, from a pure whistle through a hollow pipe to a reedy buzz.

params.name: Chirp
params.description: Breaks each steady voice into its own slow train of soft calls. At zero the voices hold; higher leaves silence between the calls.

params.name: Octaves
params.description: How many of the voices sit an octave above or below the note instead of on it. A change is heard from the next key press.

params.name: Leave
params.description: How long the voices take to scatter after a key is let go, drifting off the note as they fade. Voices already leaving keep the time they left with.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far the voices spread from left to right. At zero they all sit in the centre.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many keys stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Each voice is one sine oscillator with a few odd harmonics whose pitch is steered by a fly-in curve, a damped random walk and a scatter on release, all drawn from seeded generators; nothing of real birdsong is modelled. It is not a model of any one instrument or product.
